about: What the launch option checker knows. Every entry names the document it was taken from (`source`, keys of `sources`). Flavours: valve (Valve's numbered Proton and Hotfix), experimental, ge, cachyos, wine (Lutris/Heroic Wine), native (Linux games); shorthands proton (the four Protons), dxvk (proton + wine), all. Status: current, retired (outdated, with replacement), discouraged (works, not recommended), experimental (works, with a warning), debug (troubleshooting only), unverified (named here, but no source read confirms it: reported as unknown). byFlavour overrides the status for one flavour (from = only from that Valve major on).

sources.valve-readme: Valve Proton README, Runtime Config Options (github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton, proton_11.0, read 2026-11-13)
sources.valve-script: Valve Proton's proton script (github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton, proton_11.0, experimental_11.0 and bleeding-edge, read 2026-11-13)
sources.ge-history: GE-Proton commit b8acd40 "proton: enable ntsync by default" (2025-07-18, first in GE-Proton10-10; PROTON_USE_NTSYNC came in d7eea5a, GE-Proton10-9)
sources.cachyos-readme: proton-cachyos README, Config Options and Retired environment variables (github.com/CachyOS/proton-cachyos, read 2026-11-13)
sources.vkd3d-readme: vkd3d-proton README, VKD3D_CONFIG and environment variables (github.com/HansKristian-Work/vkd3d-proton, read 2026-11-13)
sources.vkd3d-source: vkd3d-proton source, include/private/config_flag_decl.h at 2576c0b (2026-11-12) and libs/vkd3d/device.c
sources.vkd3d-history: vkd3d-proton commits 5f319d3 (2026-05-27, i_want_broken_descriptor_heap renamed to descriptor_heap) and de580e7 (2026-11-04, descriptor heap made the default, flag replaced by no_descriptor_heap)
sources.dxvk-source: DXVK source: dxvk.conf and the environment variables read in src/ (github.com/doitsujin/dxvk, master, read 2026-11-13)
sources.nvidia-readme: NVIDIA driver README 580.95.05, OpenGL environment variables (download.nvidia.com, read 2026-11-13)
sources.wine-manual: wine(1) manual, WINEDLLOVERRIDES (not re-read 2026-11-13; long-standing syntax)

entries.name: PROTON_LOG
entries.explanation: Writes a Proton debug log to steam-<appid>.log in your home folder (or PROTON_LOG_DIR). 1 logs the default channels; a list of Wine debug channels can be given instead. Logs slow the game down and grow big, so remove it when you are done.

entries.name: PROTON_LOG_DIR
entries.explanation: The folder for PROTON_LOG's log files (your home folder by default). Does nothing without PROTON_LOG.

entries.name: PROTON_WAIT_ATTACH
entries.explanation: Waits for a debugger to attach before the game starts. Only for developers: the game seems to hang without one.

entries.name: PROTON_CRASH_REPORT_DIR
entries.explanation: Writes crash logs into this folder. Old logs are never cleaned up, so it can fill the disk over time.

entries.name: PROTON_USE_WINED3D
entries.explanation: Uses Wine's OpenGL-based renderer (wined3d) instead of the Vulkan-based DXVK for Direct3D 9 to 11. Usually much slower; only for games that break with DXVK or graphics cards without Vulkan.

entries.name: PROTON_NO_D3D11
entries.explanation: Hides Direct3D 11 from the game, for D3D11 games that can fall back to D3D9 and run better with it.

entries.name: PROTON_NO_D3D10
entries.explanation: Hides Direct3D 10 (and DXGI) from the game, for D3D10 games that can fall back to D3D9 and run better with it.

entries.name: PROTON_NO_D3D12
entries.explanation: Meant to turn off Direct3D 12. Listed in GE-Proton's README, but GE's proton script does not read it.

entries.name: PROTON_NO_D3D9
entries.explanation: Meant to turn off Direct3D 9. Listed in GE-Proton's README, but GE's proton script does not read it.

entries.name: PROTON_DXVK_D3D8
entries.explanation: Uses DXVK's Direct3D 8 for old D3D8 games instead of Wine's own.

entries.name: PROTON_NO_FSYNC
entries.explanation: Turns off fsync, Proton's futex-based synchronisation. Only for troubleshooting a game that hangs or stutters with it.

entries.name: PROTON_NO_ESYNC
entries.explanation: Turns off esync, Proton's older eventfd-based synchronisation. Only for troubleshooting.

valve.note: Valve's README marks it obsolete from Proton 11.0.

experimental.note: Valve's README marks it obsolete from Proton 11.0.

cachyos.note: proton-cachyos is based on Proton 11, where Valve marks it obsolete; its README no longer lists it.

entries.name: PROTON_NO_NTSYNC
entries.explanation: Turns off NTSync, the kernel's Windows-style synchronisation driver that current Protons use by default when /dev/ntsync is there. Only for troubleshooting a game that hangs or crashes with it; NTSync itself usually makes games smoother.

entries.name: PROTON_USE_NTSYNC
entries.note: NTSync is the default now: GE-Proton from 10-10 (only GE-Proton10-9 had this switch) and proton-cachyos from 11.0-20260428; Valve's Proton 11 uses it by default too. PROTON_NO_NTSYNC turns it off.
entries.explanation: Turned on NTSync in a few older Proton builds. Current builds use NTSync by default when /dev/ntsync is there.

entries.name: HOST_LC_ALL
entries.explanation: Sets the game's language and region settings (a locale such as ja_JP.UTF-8). Use it instead of LC_ALL.

entries.name: PROTON_DISABLE_NVAPI
entries.explanation: Turns off NVAPI, the library through which Windows games find NVIDIA features such as DLSS and Reflex. Only for games that crash with it.

entries.name: PROTON_FORCE_NVAPI
entries.explanation: Makes NVAPI start even on a non-NVIDIA driver, reporting a made-up NVIDIA driver version. Only for special cases.

entries.name: PROTON_ENABLE_NVAPI
entries.note: Current Protons turn NVAPI on by themselves (their proton script sets DXVK_ENABLE_NVAPI unless PROTON_DISABLE_NVAPI is set). GE-Proton's README still lists it, but neither Valve's nor GE's script reads it any more.
entries.explanation: Turned on NVAPI (DLSS, Reflex) in older Protons. Not needed any more: NVAPI is on by default.

entries.name: PROTON_FORCE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE
entries.explanation: Lets 32-bit games use more than 2 GB of memory. On by default already.

entries.name: PROTON_HEAP_DELAY_FREE
entries.explanation: Frees some memory later than asked, to work around games that use memory after freeing it (crashes). Only for games known to need it.

entries.name: PROTON_HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY
entries.explanation: Fills newly given memory with zeros, a workaround for games that read memory they never set. Only for games known to need it.

entries.name: PROTON_SET_GAME_DRIVE
entries.explanation: Adds a drive S: pointing to the Steam library the game is in, for games or launchers that need the game on a drive letter.

entries.name: PROTON_SET_STEAM_DRIVE
entries.explanation: Adds a drive letter pointing to Steam's own folder, for games that need it.

entries.name: PROTON_OLD_GL_STRING
entries.explanation: Shortens the OpenGL extension list for old games that crash on a very long one.

entries.name: WINE_DO_NOT_CREATE_DXGI_DEVICE_MANAGER
entries.explanation: Works around video playback problems (e.g. pink-tinted videos) in some games.

entries.name: WINE_DISABLE_VULKAN_OPWR
entries.explanation: Turns off Vulkan rendering into other processes' windows, which sometimes shows a frame late on Wayland.

entries.name: PROTON_HIDE_NVIDIA_GPU
entries.explanation: Reports an NVIDIA card as an AMD card, for games that need Windows-only NVIDIA driver features otherwise. 0 makes sure it is reported as NVIDIA.

entries.name: PROTON_HIDE_INTEL_GPU
entries.explanation: Hides an Intel graphics card from the game.

entries.name: PROTON_HIDE_APU
entries.explanation: Hides that the graphics are built into the processor (an APU), for games that misbehave on them.

entries.name: PROTON_NO_XIM
entries.explanation: Stops using the X input method, so every key press (dead keys too) reaches the game. Leave it off for Chinese, Japanese or Korean input.

entries.name: PROTON_USE_WOW64
entries.explanation: Runs 32-bit Windows programs through Wine's newer WoW64 mode.

entries.name: WINE_FULLSCREEN_INTEGER_SCALING
entries.explanation: Scales low resolutions up by whole numbers, for sharp pixels in pixel-art games.

entries.name: WINE_USE_KWIN_HACKS
entries.explanation: KDE-specific window workarounds. Valve says they help only with KDE older than 6.4 on Wayland or older than 6.6 on X11.

entries.name: PROTON_USE_XALIA
entries.explanation: Xalia adds controller support to some mouse-and-keyboard menus. 1 turns it on, 0 off; by default Proton decides by itself.

entries.name: FNA3D_FORCE_DRIVER
entries.explanation: Chooses the renderer of FNA games (D3D11 is the documented value).

entries.name: PROTON_USE_SECCOMP
entries.explanation: An old DRM workaround. Valve marks it obsolete since Proton 5.13.

entries.name: PROTON_USE_D9VK
entries.explanation: Used DXVK for Direct3D 9 in old Protons; DXVK does that by default since Proton 5.0.

entries.name: PROTON_DISABLE_HIDRAW
entries.explanation: Stops Wine from reading controllers directly (hidraw), so they go through SDL or Steam Input instead. 1 for all controllers, or a list of vendor/product ids like 0x054C/0x0CE6. Helps when a controller is seen twice or its buttons are wrong.

entries.name: PROTON_ENABLE_HIDRAW
entries.explanation: Meant to let Wine read some controllers directly. Not in the current Proton READMEs or scripts read here.

entries.name: PROTON_PREFER_SDL
entries.explanation: Reads controllers through SDL instead of hidraw or Steam Input. Can help with controllers that are not recognised, or with Wine's Wayland driver.

entries.name: PROTON_NO_STEAMINPUT
entries.explanation: Listed in proton-cachyos's README without a description; by its name it keeps Steam Input away from the game.

entries.name: PROTON_ENABLE_WAYLAND
entries.warning: Wine's Wayland driver is experimental: launchers (Battle.net, EA App, Ubisoft Connect) may show a white window, controllers may need PROTON_USE_SDL=1. When reporting a problem, check whether it happens without it.
entries.note: Valve's Protons do not include Wine's Wayland driver.
entries.explanation: Runs the game as a native Wayland window instead of through XWayland. Can give lower latency and, with GE-Proton, automatic HDR.

entries.name: PROTON_ENABLE_HDR
entries.explanation: Turned on HDR in Proton builds with Wine's Wayland driver.

cachyos.note: Removed from proton-cachyos; use DXVK_HDR=1 (plus ENABLE_HDR_WSI=1 on NVIDIA drivers older than 595).

ge.note: GE-Proton detects HDR by itself now. Setting 1 no longer forces HDR (PROTON_FORCE_HDR=1 does); 0 still turns HDR off.

entries.name: PROTON_USE_HDR
entries.note: GE-Proton detects HDR by itself now. Setting 1 no longer forces HDR (PROTON_FORCE_HDR=1 does); 0 still turns HDR off.
entries.explanation: An older HDR switch of GE-Proton.

entries.name: PROTON_FORCE_HDR
entries.warning: Only on screens that can really show HDR: on an SDR screen colours look washed out and some games hang.
entries.explanation: Reports every screen as HDR to games under Wine's Wayland driver, e.g. when KDE's SDR brightness is set to the screen's peak and the game would otherwise only offer SDR.

entries.name: DXVK_HDR
entries.explanation: Tells the game that Windows' HDR mode is on, so it offers HDR. The screen and the desktop must have HDR on too. proton-cachyos uses it as its HDR switch.

ge.note: GE-Proton detects HDR by itself; its README says to remove DXVK_HDR=1 for automatic detection.

entries.name: DXVK_NO_HDR
entries.explanation: Turns HDR off even where it would be turned on by itself.

entries.name: ENABLE_HDR_WSI
entries.explanation: Turns on the Vulkan HDR layer (vk-hdr-layer) for this game, which lets games show HDR through XWayland. proton-cachyos's README says it may be needed together with DXVK_HDR=1 on NVIDIA drivers older than 595.

entries.name: PROTON_FSR4_UPGRADE
entries.explanation: Upgrades games that have FSR 3.1 to FSR 4 (AMD's newer upscaler). The Proton build downloads the FSR4 DLL (amdxcffx64.dll) itself on start. 1 takes the latest known-good version, or give one like 4.0.1.

entries.name: PROTON_FSR4_RDNA3_UPGRADE
entries.explanation: An older FSR 4 switch for RDNA3 cards. GE-Proton says it has no effect now; PROTON_FSR4_UPGRADE covers RDNA3.

entries.name: PROTON_FSR4_INDICATOR
entries.explanation: Shows the FSR 4 watermark in the top left corner, to check that FSR 4 is in use.

entries.name: PROTON_MLFG_UPGRADE
entries.explanation: Turns on AMD's machine-learning frame generation with FSR 4 (4.0.3 or newer).

entries.name: PROTON_FSR3_UPGRADE
entries.explanation: Listed in GE-Proton's README without a description.

entries.name: PROTON_DLSS_UPGRADE
entries.explanation: Uses newer DLSS DLLs than the game ships, with the latest DLSS preset. The Proton build downloads the DLSS DLLs itself on start. 1 takes the newest, or give a version like 310.2.

entries.name: PROTON_DLSS_INDICATOR
entries.explanation: Shows the DLSS overlay in the bottom left corner, to check which DLSS version runs.

entries.name: PROTON_XESS_UPGRADE
entries.explanation: Listed in the proton-cachyos and GE-Proton READMEs without a description.

entries.name: PROTON_FFX3_UPGRADE
entries.explanation: Listed in proton-cachyos's README without a description.

entries.name: PROTON_FFX4_UPGRADE
entries.explanation: Listed in proton-cachyos's README without a description.

entries.name: PROTON_STREAMLINE_UPGRADE
entries.explanation: Downloads a newer NVIDIA Streamline for games whose copy is too old for the driver's DLSS overrides (e.g. multi frame generation).

entries.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS
entries.warning: Only when a game needs it: not with PROTON_USE_WOW64=1, and 32-bit games on RTX 4000/5000 cards may run badly (PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS_NO_32BIT=1 helps).
entries.explanation: Adds replacements for NVIDIA libraries Proton lacks (CUDA, NVENC, NVML, OptiX), e.g. for hardware PhysX.

entries.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS_NO_32BIT
entries.explanation: With PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS: only the 64-bit libraries, for RTX 4000/5000 cards that run 32-bit games badly with them.

entries.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_NVCUDA
entries.explanation: Only the CUDA replacement of PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS.

entries.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_NVENC
entries.explanation: Only the NVENC (video encoder) replacement of PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS.

entries.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_NVML
entries.explanation: The NVML replacement (GPU temperature and load for the game). On by default in proton-cachyos; 0 turns it off.

entries.name: PROTON_NVIDIA_NVOPTIX
entries.explanation: Only the OptiX replacement of PROTON_NVIDIA_LIBS.

entries.name: PROTON_NO_WM_DECORATION
entries.explanation: Turns off the desktop's window frame for the game and uses Wine's own.

entries.name: PROTON_USE_PIPEWIRE
entries.explanation: Wine's PipeWire sound driver, on by default in proton-cachyos. 0 goes back to the PulseAudio driver if sound crackles or is missing.

entries.name: WINE_AUDIO_DRIVER
entries.explanation: The sound drivers Wine may use, in order (default pipewire,pulse,alsa).

entries.name: WINEALSA_CHANNELS
entries.explanation: Number of speakers for Wine's ALSA driver (2, 4, 6 for 5.1, 8 for 7.1); 2 turns off spatial sound.

entries.name: WINEALSA_SPATIAL
entries.explanation: Mixes spatial sound down properly with Wine's ALSA driver; only if spatial sound is wrong with WINEALSA_CHANNELS.

entries.name: WINE_BLOCK_HOSTS
entries.explanation: A list of internet hosts the game may not connect to (up to 16).

entries.name: WINEPULSE_FAST_POLLING
entries.explanation: Helped against sound crackling with the old default sound driver; removed from proton-cachyos.

entries.name: PROTON_LOCAL_SHADER_CACHE
entries.explanation: Keeps a shader cache per game in the Steam library (shadercache/<appid>) even with Steam's shader pre-caching off, so the game stutters less after the first run.

entries.name: PROTON_ENABLE_MEDIACONV
entries.explanation: Proton's media converter for game videos.

cachyos.note: proton-cachyos: "For debugging purposes, do not use."

entries.name: PROTON_MEDIA_FORCE_GST
entries.explanation: Plays game videos through GStreamer; fixes cutscene video or sound in some games.

entries.name: PROTON_MEDIA_USE_GST
entries.explanation: Renamed to PROTON_MEDIA_FORCE_GST; most videos play without it now.

entries.name: PROTON_GST_VIDEO_ORIENTATION
entries.explanation: Turns game videos played through GStreamer (values as GStreamer's videoflip).

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX
entries.explanation: Turns on DXVK-NVAPI's Vulkan Reflex layer, for NVIDIA Reflex in Vulkan games. Off by default because it can disturb other Vulkan programs.

entries.name: PROTON_VKREFLEX
entries.explanation: proton-cachyos's old switch for the Vulkan Reflex layer; DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX does this now.

entries.name: LOW_LATENCY_LAYER
entries.explanation: Turns on low_latency_layer, a Vulkan layer meant to lower input lag.

entries.name: PROTON_USE_OPTISCALER
entries.warning: Work in progress and not for every game; problems with it must not be reported to OptiScaler.
entries.explanation: Puts OptiScaler into the game, which can swap the game's upscaler (DLSS, FSR, XeSS) for another.

entries.name: PROTON_OPTISCALER_NAME
entries.explanation: Which DLL OptiScaler is put in as (dxgi.dll by default).

entries.name: PROTON_OPTISCALER_CONFIG
entries.warning: Changes OptiScaler.ini for good and removes its comments.
entries.explanation: Settings written into OptiScaler.ini, as section.option=value separated by semicolons.

entries.name: PROTON_DISCORD_BRIDGE
entries.explanation: Lets the game show what you play in Discord (rpc-bridge).

entries.name: PROTON_DXVK_SAREK
entries.warning: Uses DXVK's async shader compilation: never with anti-cheat or multiplayer games.
entries.explanation: Uses the DXVK-Sarek fork for old graphics cards without full Vulkan 1.3.

entries.name: PROTON_DXVK_LOWLATENCY
entries.explanation: Uses the dxvk-low-latency fork, with frame pacing meant to lower input lag.

entries.name: PROTON_VKD3D_LOWLATENCY
entries.explanation: Uses the vkd3d-low-latency fork for Direct3D 12, with frame pacing and Reflex meant to lower input lag; read its limitations first.

entries.name: PROTON_D7VK_DDRAW
entries.explanation: Uses D7VK's ddraw.dll for DirectX 7 and older games.

entries.name: PROTON_VKD3D_HEAP
entries.note: A proton-cachyos switch for an extra vkd3d-proton build with descriptor heap. Removed: proton-cachyos's vkd3d-proton has descriptor heap now and VKD3D_CONFIG=descriptor_heap alone turns it on. Valve's and GE's proton scripts never read it.
entries.explanation: Used an extra vkd3d-proton build with the new descriptor heap code in proton-cachyos 10.

entries.name: WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR
entries.explanation: Upscales games that run below the screen's resolution with AMD FSR 1 in Wine (Vulkan games, DXVK and vkd3d-proton included).

entries.name: WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR_STRENGTH
entries.explanation: Sharpening for WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR, 0 (sharpest) to 5.

entries.name: WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR_CUSTOM_MODE
entries.explanation: A made-up screen size (WIDTHxHEIGHT) for WINE_FULLSCREEN_FSR, for games that always render at the screen's size.

entries.name: WINE_DISABLE_EXE_ASLR
entries.explanation: Loads the game's program at its preferred address, for some 32-bit programs that need it.

entries.name: PROTON_ENABLE_WINEBTH
entries.explanation: Turns on Wine's Bluetooth driver, for Bluetooth LE devices such as smart trainers in Zwift.

entries.name: WAYLANDDRV_PRIMARY_MONITOR
entries.explanation: The screen Wine's Wayland driver treats as the main one (e.g. DP-1).

entries.name: PROTON_USE_X11_EXCLUSIVE
entries.explanation: Under Wine's Wayland driver, runs only this program (e.g. Launcher.exe) through X11.

entries.name: COPYPREFIX
entries.explanation: Steam Deck helper: copies the game's prefix and shader cache between the SD card and the internal drive.

entries.name: DXVK_HUD
entries.explanation: Shows DXVK's overlay (frame rate, GPU, memory, shader compiling...) in Direct3D 8 to 11 games; a comma list of what to show, or 1 for GPU and frame rate.

entries.name: DXVK_LOG_LEVEL
entries.explanation: How much DXVK writes to its log.

entries.name: DXVK_LOG_PATH
entries.explanation: Folder for DXVK's log files; none turns the files off.

entries.name: DXVK_DEBUG
entries.explanation: DXVK's debugging modes; slows the game down.

entries.name: DXVK_CONFIG
entries.explanation: DXVK settings in the form of dxvk.conf, separated by semicolons (e.g. "dxgi.maxFrameRate = 60").

entries.name: DXVK_CONFIG_FILE
entries.explanation: Path of a dxvk.conf file with DXVK settings for this game.

entries.name: DXVK_FILTER_DEVICE_NAME
entries.explanation: Makes DXVK use the graphics card whose Vulkan name contains this text. A wrong name leaves the game without any card.

entries.name: DXVK_SHADER_CACHE
entries.explanation: 0 turns off DXVK's own shader cache (more stutter); only for troubleshooting.

entries.name: DXVK_SHADER_CACHE_PATH
entries.explanation: Folder for DXVK's shader cache.

entries.name: DXVK_ENABLE_NVAPI
entries.explanation: Stops DXVK from reporting an NVIDIA card as AMD, so NVAPI (DLSS, Reflex) can work. Current Protons set it by themselves.

entries.name: DXVK_FRAME_RATE
entries.note: DXVK itself does not read DXVK_FRAME_RATE (its limit is dxgi.maxFrameRate / d3d9.maxFrameRate, e.g. DXVK_CONFIG="dxgi.maxFrameRate = 60"); GE-Proton's script turns it into that setting.
entries.explanation: Limits the frame rate of Direct3D 9 to 11 games. DXVK's own docs prefer MangoHud's or Gamescope's limiter.

entries.name: DXVK_ASYNC
entries.note: DXVK has no async option and does not read DXVK_ASYNC; it belonged to async forks of DXVK. DXVK's graphics pipeline library support is its answer to shader stutter.
entries.explanation: Compiled shaders in the background in old async forks of DXVK; risky with anti-cheat.

entries.name: VKD3D_CONFIG

notes.descriptor_heap: Turns on vkd3d-proton's new descriptor heap code (Vulkan's VK_EXT_descriptor_heap), which fixes crashes in some games, e.g. on NVIDIA 595 drivers. An opt-in flag since 2026-05 (named i_want_broken_descriptor_heap before); since 2026-11-04 vkd3d-proton's development version uses descriptor heap by default and no longer knows this flag (no_descriptor_heap turns it off). Builds with that change will not need it.
notes.enable_experimental_features: Not in vkd3d-proton's README, but in its source: turns on unfinished Direct3D 12 features (e.g. Shader Model 6.7 or work graphs on drivers that lack what they need). Can make a game start that needs them, and can cause rendering errors.
notes.force_static_cbv: An unsafe speed hack for NVIDIA cards (vkd3d-proton README).
notes.single_queue: No asynchronous compute or transfer queues; for troubleshooting.
notes.no_upload_hvv: Keeps upload memory out of resizable-BAR video memory, which can free video memory at some speed cost.
notes.dxr: Forces ray tracing on even where vkd3d-proton considers it unsafe.
notes.no_descriptor_heap: Turns the descriptor heap code off again where it is the default.
notes.vk_debug: Vulkan debugging and validation; slow, for developers.
notes.skip_application_workarounds: Skips vkd3d-proton's per-game fixes; for debugging.
notes.breadcrumbs: Debugging help for GPU crashes; slower.

uncertain.force_bindless_texel_buffer: Proton's vkd3dbindlesstb setting puts it in, but it is not in vkd3d-proton's current flag list.

entries.explanation: A comma list of vkd3d-proton (Direct3D 12) options. Most are for debugging or for single games.

entries.name: VKD3D_DEBUG
entries.explanation: How much vkd3d-proton writes to its log.

entries.name: VKD3D_LOG_FILE
entries.explanation: Writes vkd3d-proton's log to this file.

entries.name: VKD3D_VULKAN_DEVICE
entries.explanation: Which graphics card vkd3d-proton uses, counted from 0.

entries.name: VKD3D_FILTER_DEVICE_NAME
entries.explanation: Makes vkd3d-proton skip graphics cards whose name lacks this text.

entries.name: VKD3D_DISABLE_EXTENSIONS
entries.explanation: Vulkan extensions vkd3d-proton must not use; for troubleshooting.

entries.name: VKD3D_SWAPCHAIN_PRESENT_MODE
entries.explanation: Forces how Direct3D 12 frames are shown (e.g. IMMEDIATE without vsync, FIFO with).

entries.name: VKD3D_FRAME_RATE
entries.explanation: Limits the frame rate of Direct3D 12 games; 0 uncaps.

entries.name: VKD3D_SHADER_CACHE_PATH
entries.explanation: Folder for vkd3d-proton's shader cache; 0 turns it off.

entries.name: VKD3D_FEATURE_LEVEL
entries.explanation: The Direct3D 12 feature level reported to the game (Proton's vkd3dfl12 sets 12_0).

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_DRIVER_VERSION
entries.explanation: The NVIDIA driver version reported to the game (e.g. 47141 for 471.41).

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_ALLOW_OTHER_DRIVERS
entries.explanation: Lets DXVK-NVAPI start on other drivers than NVIDIA's own (or NVK).

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_DISABLE_ENTRYPOINTS
entries.explanation: NVAPI functions to hide from the game.

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_DRS_SETTINGS
entries.explanation: NVIDIA driver profile settings for the game (setting=value pairs, e.g. DLSS presets).

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_DRS_
entries.explanation: One NVIDIA driver profile setting by name (e.g. DXVK_NVAPI_DRS_NGX_DLSS_FG_OVERRIDE=on).

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_GPU_ARCH
entries.explanation: The NVIDIA card generation reported to the game.

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_LOG_LEVEL
entries.explanation: DXVK-NVAPI's logging; trace slows the game a lot.

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_LOG_PATH
entries.explanation: Folder for DXVK-NVAPI's log file.

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_SET_NGX_DEBUG_OPTIONS
entries.explanation: NVIDIA NGX debug settings (e.g. the DLSS indicator).

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_D3D12_NV_SHADER_EXTN
entries.explanation: Experimental support for NVIDIA shader extensions in Direct3D 12 games.

entries.name: DXVK_NVAPI_FAKE_VKREFLEX
entries.explanation: Lets Vulkan Reflex start without the layer, without lowering latency.

entries.name: DISABLE_DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX
entries.explanation: Turns the Vulkan Reflex layer off even when DXVK_NVAPI_VKREFLEX=1 is set.

entries.name: RADV_PERFTEST
entries.explanation: Experimental options of Mesa's AMD Vulkan driver (RADV). Mostly for testing; a flag that became default may do nothing.

entries.name: RADV_DEBUG
entries.explanation: Debugging options of Mesa's AMD Vulkan driver; many make games slower. For troubleshooting.

entries.name: MESA_SHADER_CACHE_MAX_SIZE
entries.explanation: Largest size of Mesa's shader cache on disk (e.g. 12G; 1 GB by default). A bigger cache means less stutter in big games. The CachyOS wiki suggests setting it for all games in ~/.config/environment.d/.

entries.name: MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DISABLE
entries.explanation: Turns Mesa's shader cache off: more stutter. For troubleshooting.

entries.name: MESA_VK_WSI_PRESENT_MODE
entries.explanation: Forces how Vulkan frames are shown with Mesa's drivers (immediate: no vsync; fifo: vsync).

entries.name: DRI_PRIME
entries.explanation: Picks which graphics card Mesa uses on computers with more than one (1 for the other card).

entries.name: GALLIUM_HUD
entries.explanation: Mesa's own overlay for OpenGL games (frame rate, CPU load, driver numbers).

entries.name: mesa_glthread
entries.explanation: Mesa's threaded OpenGL. Not on Mesa's environment variable page; it is a driver setting that Mesa may also take from the environment.

entries.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_SKIP_CLEANUP
entries.explanation: Stops NVIDIA's driver from cleaning up its shader cache when it grows past its size limit, so big games do not rebuild shaders (and stutter) again. Used in the CachyOS wiki's launch option example.

entries.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_SIZE
entries.explanation: Size of NVIDIA's shader cache in bytes (the CachyOS wiki suggests 12000000000). Set it for all games in ~/.config/environment.d/: with it only in one game, the cache is trimmed again when another game runs.

entries.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE
entries.explanation: Turns NVIDIA's OpenGL shader cache on or off.

entries.name: __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_PATH
entries.explanation: Folder for NVIDIA's shader cache.

entries.name: __GL_SYNC_TO_VBLANK
entries.explanation: 0 turns vsync off for OpenGL games on NVIDIA (1, on, is the default).

entries.name: __GL_THREADED_OPTIMIZATIONS
entries.explanation: Moves some OpenGL driver work to a second thread; helps some CPU-bound OpenGL games, breaks others.

entries.name: PRESSURE_VESSEL_IMPORT_OPENXR_1_RUNTIMES
entries.explanation: Lets a game inside Steam's runtime container use the system's OpenXR runtime (e.g. WiVRn or Monado), for VR. Does nothing for a game without VR.

entries.name: MANGOHUD
entries.explanation: Turns MangoHud's overlay on for Vulkan games (the mangohud wrapper covers OpenGL too).

entries.name: MANGOHUD_CONFIG
entries.explanation: MangoHud settings separated by commas (e.g. fps_limit=60); they win over the config file.

entries.name: MANGOHUD_CONFIGFILE
entries.explanation: Path of a MangoHud config file for this game.

entries.name: MANGOHUD_DLSYM
entries.explanation: 0 turns off MangoHud's dlsym hooking for OpenGL games (on by default).

entries.name: SDL_VIDEODRIVER
entries.explanation: Picks SDL's video backend (e.g. wayland or x11) for Linux games that use SDL. Windows games under Proton or Wine use SDL's Windows backend, so it does nothing for them.

entries.name: WINEDLLOVERRIDES
entries.explanation: Chooses native (n, the game's own) or built-in (b, Wine's) DLLs, e.g. "dxgi=n,b" for mods like ReShade; an empty mode turns a DLL off. Entries are separated by semicolons.

entries.name: WINEDEBUG
entries.explanation: Wine's debug channels; -all turns Wine's messages off.

entries.name: WINEPREFIX
entries.note: Proton sets the prefix itself (Steam's compatdata folder).
entries.explanation: The folder of the Windows environment (prefix) Wine runs the game in.

entries.name: PROTON_VERB
entries.explanation: How the Proton script runs the game (e.g. waitforexitandrun, which lets protonfixes work in Lutris).

entries.name: LD_PRELOAD
entries.warning: An empty value also turns off the Steam overlay.
entries.explanation: Libraries loaded into the game first. The CachyOS wiki suggests LD_PRELOAD="" against stutter caused by Steam's game recorder.

entries.name: gamemoderun
entries.explanation: Feral's GameMode: asks the system for full processor speed and priority while the game runs.

entries.name: game-performance
entries.explanation: CachyOS's wrapper: switches power-profiles-daemon to the performance profile (and a running scx scheduler to its gaming mode) while the game runs, and back afterwards. Needs power-profiles-daemon.

entries.name: mangohud
entries.explanation: Shows frame rate, frame times and temperatures over the game (Vulkan and OpenGL).

entries.name: gamescope
entries.explanation: Runs the game inside Valve's small compositor, at a size and refresh rate of your choice, with its own upscaling, frame limit and HDR.

entries.name: prime-run
entries.explanation: Starts the game on the NVIDIA card of a laptop with two graphics chips.

entries.name: obs-gamecapture
entries.explanation: Lets OBS record the game directly through obs-vkcapture, with less load than screen capture.

entries.name: dlss-swapper
entries.explanation: CachyOS's wrapper that makes the game use the latest DLSS preset; dlss-swapper-dll also swaps in a newer DLSS DLL you put in place.

entries.name: dlss-swapper-dll
entries.explanation: CachyOS's wrapper for when dlss-swapper fails: uses a newer nvngx_dlss.dll you replaced by hand.

entries.name: env
entries.explanation: Sets the settings after it for the game (env NAME=value).

entries.name: taskset
entries.explanation: Limits the game to some processor cores.

entries.name: nice
entries.explanation: Runs the game at another processor priority.

entries.name: strace
entries.explanation: Records every system call of the game, for debugging; slows it down.

entries.name: --in-process-gpu
entries.explanation: For Electron/CEF launchers (Battle.net, EA App, Ubisoft Connect) that show a white window under Wine's Wayland driver.
